sections.heading: What Is an Insulated Glass Unit and Why Does It Fail?
sections.body: An insulated glass unit, commonly called an IGU or double-pane unit, consists of two or more panes of glass separated by a spacer and sealed around the perimeter to trap an insulating gas — typically argon or air — between the panes. This sealed air space is what gives modern windows their thermal performance advantage over single-pane glass. Over time, however, the perimeter seal can break down due to age, temperature cycling, moisture infiltration, or physical stress. Once the seal fails, outside air and humidity enter the gap, causing the familiar fogging or condensation that appears between the panes and cannot be wiped away. In Washington DC's climate, where summers are hot and humid and winters can bring sharp cold snaps, thermal stress on window seals is a real factor. Properties from Capitol Hill office buildings to residential neighborhoods in Woodley Park can experience IGU failures as windows age. Replacing the failed unit rather than the entire window frame is usually a cost-effective approach that restores performance without a full window replacement.

sections.heading: Choosing the Right Glass for Your IGU Replacement
sections.body: Not all insulated glass units are identical, and the right specification for your replacement unit depends on your building type, window orientation, and performance goals. Standard clear IGUs are a common and economical choice for many applications, but there are other options worth understanding. Low-emissivity coatings, often called low-e coatings, are applied to one surface of the glass and help reduce heat transfer through the unit, which can be beneficial in both hot summers and cold winters. Tempered glass is commonly used in locations such as sidelites, doors, and low installations. Laminated glass interlayers are an option some property owners choose for added durability in certain applications. Specialty tints and coatings can also address glare or privacy concerns in specific situations. Our team will discuss the available options with you based on your property's needs and help you select a unit that fits your budget and performance expectations. We do not pressure clients toward unnecessary upgrades, but we do ensure you have the information needed to make an informed decision.

faq.q: How do I know if my double-pane window needs an IGU replacement rather than a full window replacement?
faq.a: If the glass itself is fogged, cracked, or showing condensation between the panes but the window frame is structurally sound with no rot, warping, or serious damage, IGU replacement is often the more cost-effective option. Our technician will assess both the glass and the frame during an on-site visit and give you an honest recommendation.

faq.q: What causes the foggy appearance between double-pane window glass?
faq.a: The fog or haze you see between panes is caused by a failed perimeter seal. When the seal breaks down, the insulating gas escapes and outside air — along with humidity — enters the space between the panes. The moisture then condenses on the interior glass surfaces where it cannot be reached for cleaning. The only lasting solution is replacing the insulated glass unit.
